claims.claim: Similar principles apply to the negative regulation of RPL3 and RPL4 mRNA levels.
claims.source: Importantly, the above-described data now permit to conclude that similar principles apply to the negative regulation of RPL3 and RPL4 mRNA levels.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion comparing the regulatory mechanisms for RPL3 and RPL4.

claims.claim: Maximal regulation of RPL3 and RPL4 mRNAs requires an additional segment of around 30 amino acids after the identified, critically important Rpl3 (F16/L17) or Rpl4 (W109) residues.
claims.source: Besides basically involving the same regulatory machinery, maximal regulation requires in both cases an additional segment of around 30 amino acids after the identified, critically important Rpl3 (F16/L17) or Rpl4 (W109) residues, suggesting that an auxiliary, yet to be unveiled feature contributes to the regulation process (see Discussion).
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion from the mapping experiments on both Rpl3 and Rpl4.

claims.claim: Nascent Rpl3 and Rpl4 harbor the signal eliciting the negative regulation of their own mRNA levels.
claims.source: Moreover, the crucial role of individual residues provides compelling evidence that nascent Rpl3 and Rpl4 harbor the signal eliciting the negative regulation of their own mRNA levels.
claims.evidence: This is an inference from the mutagenesis data showing specific residues are critical.

claims.claim: Co-translational capturing of Rpl3 or Rpl4 by its respective dedicated chaperone precludes their recognition by the regulatory machinery.
claims.source: Finally, the immediate proximity or overlap of the Rrb1- or Acl4-binding site with residues that are needed for potent regulation advocates a model in which co-translational capturing of Rpl3 or Rpl4 by its respective dedicated chaperone would preclude their recognition by the regulatory machinery.
claims.evidence: This is a model proposed based on the mapping data showing overlap of binding sites.

claims.claim: Overexpression of Rrb1 results in a more than 2.5-fold increase in RPL3 mRNA levels both in wild-type and ∆rrb1 cells.
claims.source: When grown at 30°C in liquid SGal-Leu medium, overexpression of Rrb1 resulted in a more than 2.5-fold increase in RPL3 mRNA levels both in wild-type and ∆rrb1 cells (Figure 6), whereas a slight decrease in RPL4 mRNA abundance could be observed.
claims.evidence: This is a result from qRT-PCR experiments shown in Figure 6.

claims.claim: Overexpression of Acl4 leads to a robust increase in RPL4 mRNA levels.
claims.source: Likewise, overexpression of Acl4 led to a similarly robust increase in RPL4 mRNA levels while, at the same time, the abundance of the RPL3 mRNA was marginally negatively affected.
claims.evidence: This is a result from qRT-PCR experiments.

claims.claim: Depletion of either Rrb1 or Acl4 results in a more than twofold decrease in RPL3 or RPL4 mRNA levels, respectively.
claims.source: Conversely, depletion of either Rrb1 or Acl4, which as expected entailed either a lethal or an sg phenotype, by growing cells for 24 hr in glucose-containing medium resulted in a more than twofold decrease in RPL3 or RPL4 mRNA levels, respectively (Figure 6).
claims.evidence: This is a result from qRT-PCR experiments shown in Figure 6.

claims.claim: The availability of the dedicated chaperone for binding to its nascent r-protein client is a crucial parameter for determining the stability of the corresponding mRNA.
claims.source: Taken together, we conclude that the availability of the dedicated chaperone for binding to its nascent r-protein client is a crucial parameter for determining the stability of the corresponding mRNA.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion from the overexpression and depletion experiments.

claims.claim: Overexpression of Rpl3 or Rpl4a from a multicopy plasmid in ∆tom1 cells results in a more severe growth defect than overexpression of Rpl26.
claims.source: While only a minor effect on growth of wild-type cells could be discerned, overexpression of Rpl3 or Rpl4a in ∆tom1 cells resulted in a more severe growth defect than overexpression of Rpl26 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A), which was previously shown to be degraded by the proteasome upon ubiquitination by Tom1 (Sung et al., 2016a; Sung et al., 2016b).
claims.evidence: This is a result from growth assays shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A, citing two references.

claims.claim: Overexpression of the BIV and W109C Rpl4a variants as well as the F16A/L17A and R19A/K20A/R21A Rpl3 variants exclusively and strongly compromises the growth of ∆tom1 cells.
claims.source: Strikingly, overexpression of the BIV and W109C Rpl4a variants as well as the F16A/L17A and R19A/K20A/R21A Rpl3 variants exclusively and strongly compromised, albeit to different extents, the growth of ∆tom1 cells, while overexpression of wild-type Rpl4a and Rpl3 only marginally affected growth (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B and C).
claims.evidence: This is a result from growth assays shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B and C.

claims.claim: Presence of the H3E mutation substantially exacerbates the impact of the Rpl3 variants harboring the F16A/L17A and R19A/K20A/R21A substitutions on growth of ∆tom1 cells.
claims.source: Notably, presence of the H3E mutation substantially exacerbated the impact of the Rpl3 variants harboring the F16A/L17A and R19A/K20A/R21A substitutions on growth of ∆tom1 cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: This is a result from growth assays shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: The BIV and W109C Rpl4a variants exhibit a higher occurrence than wild-type Rpl4a in aggregates of ∆tom1 cells.
claims.source: In good correlation with the observed expression levels, the two Rpl4a variants, which could already be detected to some extent in the insoluble fraction of wild-type cells, exhibited a higher occurrence than wild-type Rpl4a in aggregates of ∆tom1 cells.
claims.evidence: This is a result from protein aggregation assays.

claims.claim: The F16A/L17A and R19A/K20A/R21A Rpl3 variants are considerably enriched in the insoluble fraction of wild-type cells compared to wild-type Rpl3.
claims.source: The two Rpl3 variants (F16A/L17A and R19A/K20A/R21A), despite being similarly abundant as wild-type Rpl3 in the total extracts, were considerably enriched in the insoluble fraction of wild-type cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 2B).
claims.evidence: This is a result from protein aggregation assays shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2B.

claims.claim: The abundance and insolubility of the F16A/L17A and R19A/K20A/R21A Rpl3 mutant proteins are substantially increased in the absence of Tom1.
claims.source: Compared to wild-type Rpl3, the abundance and, even more markedly, the insolubility of the two Rpl3 mutant proteins, especially of the F16A/L17A variant, were substantially increased in the absence of Tom1.
claims.evidence: This is a result from protein aggregation assays comparing wild-type and ∆tom1 cells.

claims.claim: Tom1-mediated clearance of excess Rpl3 and Rpl4 is required to efficiently prevent their aggregation.
claims.source: Altogether, the above findings provide evidence that Tom1-mediated clearance of excess Rpl3 and Rpl4 is required to efficiently prevent their aggregation.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion from the aggregation experiments in Tom1-deficient cells.

claims.claim: The detrimental impact of Rpl3 and Rpl4 on cell growth only sets in once a certain threshold of aggregation has been exceeded.
claims.source: Moreover, given that wild-type Rpl3 and Rpl4a exert a dosage-dependent negative effect on the growth of ∆tom1 cells and also considering that only Rpl3 and Rpl4a variants inducibly expressed in a deregulated fashion, thus exhibiting higher abundance than their wild-type counterparts in the insoluble fraction, severely affect the growth of cells lacking Tom1, it is reasonable to assume that the detrimental impact on cell growth only sets in once a certain threshold of aggregation has been exceeded.
claims.evidence: This is an inference from the dose-dependent effects observed in the experiments.

claims.claim: The mutant Rpl3 and Rpl4a variants display in most ∆tom1 cells a strong fluorescence signal in the nucle(ol)ar compartment.
claims.source: Conversely, the mutant Rpl3 and Rpl4a variants displayed in most ∆tom1 cells a strong fluorescence signal in the nucle(ol)ar compartment.
claims.evidence: This is a result from fluorescence microscopy experiments.

claims.claim: The induced overexpression of Rpl3 or Rpl4 leads to their aggregation within the nucle(ol)ar compartment of cells lacking Tom1.
claims.source: Taken together, we conclude that the induced overexpression of Rpl3 or Rpl4 leads to their aggregation within the nucle(ol)ar compartment of cells lacking the E3 ubiquitin ligase Tom1.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion from the fluorescence microscopy experiments.

claims.claim: Cells simultaneously lacking Caf130, Not1's N-terminal CaInD domain, or either of the two NAC subunits and Tom1 are inviable.
claims.source: Notably, the absence of Caf130, Not1's N-terminal CaInD domain, or either of the two NAC subunits, which all cause the deregulated expression of both Rpl3 and Rpl4, conferred synthetic lethality to cells lacking Tom1 (Figure 7B, Figure 7—figure supplement 3B–G).
claims.evidence: This is a result from genetic analysis shown in Figure 7B and Figure 7—figure supplement 3B–G.

claims.claim: Cells simultaneously lacking Cal4 and Tom1 are inviable.
claims.source: Even more remarkably, cells simultaneously lacking Cal4, which only increases RPL4 but not RPL3 mRNA levels, and Tom1 were also inviable (Figure 7B, Figure 7—figure supplement 3A), suggesting that deregulated expression of endogenous Rpl4 is already sufficient to confer lethality when excess r-proteins are not degraded by Tom1-dependent clearance.
claims.evidence: This is a result from genetic analysis shown in Figure 7B and Figure 7—figure supplement 3A.

claims.claim: Deregulated expression of endogenous Rpl4 is sufficient to confer lethality when excess r-proteins are not degraded by Tom1-dependent clearance.
claims.source: Even more remarkably, cells simultaneously lacking Cal4, which only increases RPL4 but not RPL3 mRNA levels, and Tom1 were also inviable (Figure 7B, Figure 7—figure supplement 3A), suggesting that deregulated expression of endogenous Rpl4 is already sufficient to confer lethality when excess r-proteins are not degraded by Tom1-dependent clearance.
claims.evidence: This is an inference from the synthetic lethality of ∆cal4/∆tom1 cells.

claims.claim: Lowering the levels of synthesized Rpl4 by deleting the RPL4A gene efficiently suppresses the synthetic lethality of ∆cal4/∆tom1 cells.
claims.source: In agreement with excess Rpl4 being directly responsible for the synergistic growth defect, deregulated Rpl4a expression, this time enabled by the presence of the BIV mutations in the genomic RPL4A copy, did not support growth upon genetic depletion of Tom1 (Figure 7—figure supplement 3H). Accordingly, lowering the levels of synthesized Rpl4, by deleting the RPL4A gene, efficiently suppressed the synthetic lethality of ∆cal4/∆tom1 cells (Figure 7B).
claims.evidence: This is a result from genetic suppression analysis shown in Figure 7B.

claims.claim: Providing Rpl4 exclusively from the RPL4B locus is not sufficient to restore growth of ∆caf130/∆tom1 cells.
claims.source: Providing Rpl4 exclusively from the RPL4B locus, however, was not sufficient to restore growth of ∆caf130/∆tom1 cells (Figure 7B), suggesting that not only excess supply of Rpl4 but also of Rpl3 is individually detrimental for cells lacking Tom1.
claims.evidence: This is a result from genetic analysis shown in Figure 7B.

claims.claim: Not only excess supply of Rpl4 but also of Rpl3 is individually detrimental for cells lacking Tom1.
claims.source: Providing Rpl4 exclusively from the RPL4B locus, however, was not sufficient to restore growth of ∆caf130/∆tom1 cells (Figure 7B), suggesting that not only excess supply of Rpl4 but also of Rpl3 is individually detrimental for cells lacking Tom1.
claims.evidence: This is an inference from the genetic analysis.

claims.claim: Only simultaneously reducing the abundance of Rpl4 and Rpl3 permits efficient growth of ∆caf130/∆tom1 cells.
claims.source: Even more importantly, only simultaneously reducing the abundance of Rpl4 and Rpl3 by deleting RPL4A and expressing Rpl3 from the weaker RPL4B promoter (Zeevi et al., 2011; Knight et al., 2014), but not solely lowering Rpl3 levels, permitted efficient growth of ∆caf130/∆tom1 cells (Figure 7C).
claims.evidence: This is a result from genetic analysis shown in Figure 7C, citing two references.

claims.claim: The moderate constant surplus supply of either Rpl3 or Rpl4 is sufficient to perturb growth and possibly also proteostasis of cells lacking Tom1.
claims.source: Together, the genetic data convincingly demonstrate that the moderate constant surplus supply, around twofold at the mRNA level, of either Rpl3 or Rpl4 is sufficient to perturb growth and possibly also proteostasis of cells lacking Tom1.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion from the genetic analysis.

claims.claim: Rpl3 appears after 8 hr in glucose-containing medium in the insoluble fraction of ∆caf130/PGAL-2xHA-TOM1 cells.
claims.source: Strikingly, Rpl3 appeared already after 8 hr in glucose-containing medium in the insoluble fraction of ∆caf130/PGAL-2xHA-TOM1 cells, and Western analysis also revealed some accumulation of Rpl4 at this time point (Figure 7D).
claims.evidence: This is a result from protein aggregation assays shown in Figure 7D.

claims.claim: After 24 hr of Tom1 depletion in ∆caf130 cells, a massive aggregation of Rpl3 and Rpl4 can be observed.
claims.source: After 24 hr of Tom1 depletion, a massive aggregation of Rpl3 and, albeit to a lesser extent, of Rpl4 could be observed.
claims.evidence: This is a result from protein aggregation assays.

claims.claim: Aggregation of Rpl3 and Rpl4 leads to an extensive perturbation of cellular proteostasis.
claims.source: Concomitantly, many additional proteins showed up in the insoluble fraction, including, as indicated by Western analysis, several r-proteins (Figure 7D), suggesting that aggregation of Rpl3 and Rpl4 leads to an extensive perturbation of cellular proteostasis.
claims.evidence: This is an inference from the observation of many proteins in the insoluble fraction shown in Figure 7D.

claims.claim: The abundance of several r-proteins is substantially decreased in the total extracts after 24 hr of Tom1 depletion in ∆caf130 cells.
claims.source: Notably, the abundance of the other directly tested r-proteins was substantially decreased in the total extracts after 24 hr of Tom1 depletion, presumably reflecting, as recently described (Albert et al., 2019), the decreased transcription of their encoding genes as a result of lower Ifh1 promoter occupancy in order to alleviate the proteotoxic burden.
claims.evidence: This is a result from Western blot analysis, citing Albert et al., 2019.

claims.claim: Depleting Tom1 for 24 hr in ∆cal4 cells results in extensive aggregation of Rpl4 and the concomitant presence of many additional proteins in the insoluble fraction.
claims.source: As expected, depleting Tom1 for 24 hr in ∆cal4 cells resulted, to a similar extent as observed above in ∆caf130 cells, in extensive aggregation of Rpl4 and the concomitant presence of many additional proteins in the insoluble fraction (Figure 7D).
claims.evidence: This is a result from protein aggregation assays shown in Figure 7D.

claims.claim: The deregulated expression of Rpl3 and/or Rpl4, in the absence of Tom1-dependent clearance, promotes their aggregation and entails a loss of overall proteostasis.
claims.source: We note that the deregulated expression of Rpl3 and/or Rpl4, in the absence of Tom1-dependent clearance of their excess occurrence, promotes their aggregation and entails a loss of overall proteostasis, which very likely accounts for the observed synthetic lethality of ∆caf130/∆tom1 and also of ∆cal4/∆tom1 cells.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion from the aggregation and genetic lethality data.

claims.claim: The two dedicated chaperones Rrb1 and Acl4 intimately cooperate with the regulatory machinery to provide optimal levels of assembly-competent Rpl3 and Rpl4.
claims.source: Taken together, we conclude that the two dedicated chaperones Rrb1 and Acl4 intimately cooperate with the regulatory machinery to provide optimal levels of assembly-competent Rpl3 and Rpl4.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion summarizing the findings of the study.

claims.claim: By perfectly balancing the de novo synthesis of Rpl3 and Rpl4, pre-60S assembly can be sustained at the highest possible rate without requiring Tom1-mediated degradation of excess Rpl3 and Rpl4.
claims.source: By perfectly balancing their de novo synthesis, pre-60S assembly can be sustained at the highest possible rate without requiring the Tom1-mediated degradation of excess Rpl3 and Rpl4, which would, as a last resort, be necessary to avoid their aggregation and, ultimately, a potentially deleterious collapse of cellular proteostasis.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the physiological significance of the regulatory mechanism.

claims.claim: The main, physiologically relevant targets of the regulatory machinery are the RPL3 and RPL4A/B mRNAs.
claims.source: Importantly, the above-described data also strongly suggest that the main, physiologically relevant targets of the regulatory machinery are the RPL3 and RPL4A/B mRNAs.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion from the specificity of the regulation observed in the study.

claims.claim: Under normal conditions, when ribosome assembly proceeds at an optimal rate, the dedicated chaperones Rrb1 and Acl4 are available in sufficient amounts to capture their nascent r-protein client Rpl3 or Rpl4, respectively, leading to a stabilization of the RPL3 or RPL4 mRNA.
claims.source: Under normal conditions, that is, when ribosome assembly proceeds at an optimal rate, the dedicated chaperones Rrb1 and Acl4 are available in sufficient amounts to capture their nascent r-protein client Rpl3 or Rpl4, respectively, as the specific chaperone-binding segment emerges from the exit tunnel on the surface of the 60S r-subunit, thereby leading to a stabilization of the RPL3 or RPL4 mRNA that is in the process of being translated.
claims.evidence: This is part of the proposed model in the Discussion section.

claims.claim: When ribosome biogenesis occurs at reduced pace and Rpl3 or Rpl4 cannot get efficiently integrated into developing pre-60S particles, Rrb1 and Acl4 get sequestered by their unassembled r-protein partner in the nucleus.
claims.source: Conversely, when ribosome biogenesis occurs at reduced pace and Rpl3 or Rpl4 cannot get efficiently integrated into the developing pre-60S particles, Rrb1 and Acl4 get sequestered by their unassembled r-protein partner in the nucleus and, therefore, can no longer bind to nascent Rpl3 or Rpl4 in a timely manner.
claims.evidence: This is part of the proposed model in the Discussion section.

claims.claim: When Rrb1 and Acl4 are sequestered, the presumed co-translational interaction of NAC with the regulation-conferring segment on Rpl3 or Rpl4 persists long enough to enable the recruitment of or transfer to the regulatory machinery.
claims.source: In this case, the presumed, co-translational interaction of NAC with the regulation-conferring segment on these two r-proteins persists long enough to enable the recruitment of or the transfer to the regulatory machinery, which, likely via the Caf1-Ccr4 deadenylase module of the Caf130-associated Ccr4-Not core complex, promotes the degradation of the physically connected RPL3 or RPL4 mRNA.
claims.evidence: This is part of the proposed model in the Discussion section.

claims.claim: The regulatory machinery likely promotes the degradation of the RPL3 or RPL4 mRNA via the Caf1-Ccr4 deadenylase module of the Caf130-associated Ccr4-Not core complex.
claims.source: In this case, the presumed, co-translational interaction of NAC with the regulation-conferring segment on these two r-proteins persists long enough to enable the recruitment of or the transfer to the regulatory machinery, which, likely via the Caf1-Ccr4 deadenylase module of the Caf130-associated Ccr4-Not core complex, promotes the degradation of the physically connected RPL3 or RPL4 mRNA.
claims.evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism of mRNA degradation in the proposed model.

claims.claim: Overexpression of Rrb1 or Acl4 leads to a further, specific increase in RPL3 or RPL4 mRNA levels, suggesting that the two dedicated chaperones are present in somewhat limiting amounts.
claims.source: The finding that overexpression of Rrb1 or Acl4 leads to a further, specific increase in RPL3 or RPL4 mRNA levels strongly suggests that the two dedicated chaperones are actually present in somewhat limiting amounts and that, even under normal growth conditions, there is a constant competition between Rrb1 or Acl4 and the regulatory machinery for binding to nascent Rpl3 or Rpl4 (Figure 6), thus, conferring high sensitivity to the regulatory process.
claims.evidence: This is an inference from the overexpression experiments shown in Figure 6.

claims.claim: Even under normal growth conditions, there is a constant competition between Rrb1 or Acl4 and the regulatory machinery for binding to nascent Rpl3 or Rpl4.
claims.source: The finding that overexpression of Rrb1 or Acl4 leads to a further, specific increase in RPL3 or RPL4 mRNA levels strongly suggests that the two dedicated chaperones are actually present in somewhat limiting amounts and that, even under normal growth conditions, there is a constant competition between Rrb1 or Acl4 and the regulatory machinery for binding to nascent Rpl3 or Rpl4 (Figure 6), thus, conferring high sensitivity to the regulatory process.
claims.evidence: This is an inference from the overexpression experiments shown in Figure 6.

claims.claim: The functional utility of dedicated chaperones can be extended to the purpose of serving as molecular rheostats that continuously sense the status of early pre-60S assembly.
claims.source: Accordingly, the functional utility of dedicated chaperones can be extended to the purpose of serving as molecular rheostats that, in the case of Rrb1 and Acl4, continuously sense the status of early pre-60S assembly by surveying the levels of free Rpl3 or Rpl4, respectively, and thereby coordinate the production of new Rpl3 and Rpl4 with their actual consumption during biogenesis of 60S r-subunits.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the functional role of dedicated chaperones based on the study's findings.

claims.claim: The meticulous adjustment of the abundance of unassembled Rpl3 and/or Rpl4 may become essential to maintain cellular proteostasis depending on the cell's proteostatic state.
claims.source: We conclude that, depending on the cell's proteostatic state, the meticulous adjustment of the abundance of unassembled Rpl3 and/or Rpl4, achieved by a properly functioning interplay between the regulatory machinery and the dedicated chaperones Rrb1 and Acl4, may become essential to maintain cellular proteostasis.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion about the physiological importance of the regulatory mechanism.

claims.claim: The autoregulatory feedback loop constitutes together with the ERISQ pathway a robust buffering system to prevent cells from experiencing the harmful impact of excess Rpl3 and/or Rpl4.
claims.source: Moreover, the here-described autoregulatory feedback loop constitutes together with the ERISQ pathway a robust buffering system to prevent cells from experiencing the harmful impact of excess Rpl3 and/or Rpl4.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of how the regulatory mechanism and ERISQ pathway work together.

claims.claim: The RPL3 and RPL4A/B genes contain category III promoters.
claims.source: Notably, the RPL3 and RPL4A/B genes contain category III promoters, and they are the RPGs whose efficient transcription, while being rather insensitive to Ifh1 depletion or the ribosome assembly stress response (RASTR), shows the highest Sfp1 dependence (Albert et al., 2019; Zencir et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This is a statement about the promoter types of RPL3 and RPL4 genes, citing two references.

claims.claim: RPL3 and RPL4A/B are the RPGs whose efficient transcription shows the highest Sfp1 dependence.
claims.source: Notably, the RPL3 and RPL4A/B genes contain category III promoters, and they are the RPGs whose efficient transcription, while being rather insensitive to Ifh1 depletion or the ribosome assembly stress response (RASTR), shows the highest Sfp1 dependence (Albert et al., 2019; Zencir et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This is a statement about the transcriptional regulation of RPL3 and RPL4 genes, citing two references.

claims.claim: The co-translational regulation of RPL3 and RPL4 mRNA levels represents an elegant mechanism to specifically reduce the de novo synthesis of Rpl3 and Rpl4 when their unassembled levels exceed the buffering capacity of the dedicated chaperones Rrb1 and Acl4.
claims.source: Accordingly, the here-described co-translational regulation of RPL3 and RPL4 mRNA levels represents an elegant mechanism to specifically reduce the de novo synthesis of Rpl3 and Rpl4 when their unassembled levels exceed, due to a perturbation of ribosome assembly, the buffering capacity of the dedicated chaperones Rrb1 and Acl4.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the functional significance of the regulatory mechanism.

claims.claim: The regulatory mechanism continuously operates under normal growth conditions.
claims.source: While the above would suggest a special relevance for rapidly responding to certain stress conditions, our data indicate that the regulatory mechanism also continuously operates under normal growth conditions.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion from the data showing regulation occurs even without stress.

claims.claim: The RPL3 and RPL4A/B transcripts are among the five RPG mRNAs exhibiting markedly shorter half-lives than all other RPG mRNAs.
claims.source: In line with a constant adjustment of their transcript levels via a regulated degradation pathway, the RPL3 and RPL4A/B transcripts are among the five RPG mRNAs exhibiting markedly shorter half-lives than all other RPG mRNAs (Wang et al., 2002).
claims.evidence: This is a statement about mRNA half-lives, citing Wang et al., 2002.

claims.claim: Both Rpl3 and Rpl4 are among the earliest assembling large subunit r-proteins, associating shortly before or after the generation of the 27SA2 pre-rRNA.
claims.source: Both Rpl3 and Rpl4, by associating shortly before or after the generation of the 27SA2 pre-rRNA, are among the earliest assembling large subunit r-proteins, and they fulfill a central role for the compaction and/or stabilization of the earliest pre-60S particles (Rosado et al., 2007; Pöll et al., 2009; Gamalinda et al., 2014; Pillet et al., 2015; Joret et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This describes the timing and importance of Rpl3 and Rpl4 assembly, citing five references.

claims.claim: Rpl3 and Rpl4 fulfill a central role for the compaction and/or stabilization of the earliest pre-60S particles.
claims.source: Both Rpl3 and Rpl4, by associating shortly before or after the generation of the 27SA2 pre-rRNA, are among the earliest assembling large subunit r-proteins, and they fulfill a central role for the compaction and/or stabilization of the earliest pre-60S particles (Rosado et al., 2007; Pöll et al., 2009; Gamalinda et al., 2014; Pillet et al., 2015; Joret et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This describes the functional role of Rpl3 and Rpl4 in ribosome assembly, citing five references.

claims.claim: The temporary nuclear storage of Rpl3 and Rpl4 in complex with their dedicated chaperone provides the required buffering capacity to rapidly respond to short-term increases in assembly demand.
claims.source: The temporary nuclear storage of Rpl3 and Rpl4 in complex with their dedicated chaperone not only provides the required buffering capacity to rapidly respond to short-term increases in assembly demand but also the means to relay and directly connect the status of early pre-60S assembly to the rate of the two r-proteins' de novo synthesis.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the functional significance of chaperone-mediated storage.

claims.claim: The temporary nuclear storage of Rpl3 and Rpl4 in complex with their dedicated chaperone provides the means to relay and directly connect the status of early pre-60S assembly to the rate of the two r-proteins' de novo synthesis.
claims.source: The temporary nuclear storage of Rpl3 and Rpl4 in complex with their dedicated chaperone not only provides the required buffering capacity to rapidly respond to short-term increases in assembly demand but also the means to relay and directly connect the status of early pre-60S assembly to the rate of the two r-proteins' de novo synthesis.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the functional significance of chaperone-mediated storage.

claims.claim: Compared to a purely transcription-based adaptation of protein levels, the uncovered regulatory mechanism has the advantage of enabling a more rapid response.
claims.source: Compared to a purely transcription-based adaptation of protein levels, the uncovered regulatory mechanism, owing to the constant supply of new RPL3 and RPL4A/B mRNAs that are then either translated or subjected to regulated degradation, has the evident advantage of enabling a more rapid response.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the advantages of the regulatory mechanism.

claims.claim: The accurate functioning of the regulatory system is instrumental to avoid the impact of both the surplus and insufficient supply of Rpl3 and/or Rpl4.
claims.source: We conclude that the accurate functioning of this regulatory system is instrumental to avoid the impact of both the surplus and insufficient supply of Rpl3 and/or Rpl4.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion about the importance of the regulatory system.

claims.claim: An involvement of one of the associated core components of the Ccr4-Not complex in mRNA degradation can be supposed.
claims.source: Considering the mandatory requirement of a physical connection with Not1 for negative regulation of RPL3 and RPL4 mRNA levels to occur, an involvement of one of the associated core components of the Ccr4-Not complex can be supposed.
claims.evidence: This is a speculation about which components mediate mRNA degradation.

claims.claim: It is highly likely that the Caf1-Ccr4 deadenylase module promotes degradation of the RPL3 and RPL4 mRNA.
claims.source: Since it is well established that the Ccr4-Not complex plays an important role in the decay of cytoplasmic mRNAs, a process that is initiated by deadenylation of the poly(A) tail (Parker, 2012), we consider it highly likely that its Caf1-Ccr4 deadenylase module promotes degradation of the RPL3 and RPL4 mRNA.
claims.evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism of mRNA degradation, citing Parker, 2012.

claims.claim: The utilization of a defined segment of the encoded nascent polypeptide constitutes an unprecedented mechanism of recruitment of the Ccr4-Not complex to a substrate mRNA.
claims.source: Notably, the utilization of a defined segment of the encoded nascent polypeptide constitutes, to the best of our knowledge, an unprecedented mechanism of recruitment of the Ccr4-Not complex to a substrate mRNA, which is more conventionally achieved through interactions with either the poly(A)-binding protein or rather general as well as specific RNA-binding proteins (Parker, 2012; Wahle and Winkler, 2013; Bresson and Tollervey, 2018), but, as recently shown, can also occur via the accommodation of the Not5-NTD in the ribosomal E-site of mRNAs displaying low codon optimality (Buschauer et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the recruitment mechanism, citing four references.

claims.claim: Heterodimeric NAC is involved in the substrate recognition process.
claims.source: The strict requirement of both NAC subunits for negative regulation indicates that heterodimeric NAC, owing to its established role as a ribosome-associated chaperone that binds nascent chains (Deuerling et al., 2019), is involved in the substrate recognition process.
claims.evidence: This is an inference from the genetic requirement for both NAC subunits, citing Deuerling et al., 2019.

claims.claim: The yeast NAC-β subunits may be responsible for establishing the initial contact with the N-terminal part of the regulation-conferring segment of nascent Rpl3 and Rpl4.
claims.source: Given that the N-terminal tail of NAC-β can insert, as seen in the cryo-EM structure of a reconstituted Caenorhabditis elegans NAC-60S complex, up to the constriction point of the polypeptide exit tunnel to sense and bind to nascent chains (Gamerdinger et al., 2019), we assume that the yeast NAC-β subunits may be responsible for establishing the initial contact with the N-terminal part of the regulation-conferring segment of nascent Rpl3 and Rpl4.
claims.evidence: This is a speculation based on structural data from C. elegans, citing Gamerdinger et al., 2019.

claims.claim: The residues following the key residues F16/L17 in Rpl3 and W109 in Rpl4 may have a propensity for stalling the nascent chain in the exit tunnel.
claims.source: Conspicuously, in both cases the residues identified as being crucial for conferring regulation, F16/L17 and W109, respectively, are followed by a segment of around 30 amino acids that is also required to confer maximal regulation. Considering that around 25–30 amino acids are generally buried within the exit tunnel (Bhushan et al., 2010; Wilson et al., 2016; Döring et al., 2017), we speculate that the residues following these key residues, especially those potentially extending from the constriction point of the tunnel to the peptidyl transferase center, may have a propensity for stalling the nascent chain in the exit tunnel.
claims.evidence: This is a speculation based on the length of the exit tunnel, citing three references.

claims.claim: Timely association with the dedicated chaperone may preclude NAC from interacting with nascent Rpl3 or Rpl4 and allow translation to proceed.
claims.source: The immediate proximity or even partial overlap of the Rrb1- or Acl4-binding site and the key residues of the regulation-conferring segment suggests that timely association with the dedicated chaperone may preclude NAC from interacting with nascent Rpl3 or Rpl4 and allow translation to proceed.
claims.evidence: This is a speculation based on the overlap of binding sites.

claims.claim: If Rpl3 or Rpl4 are not swiftly captured by their dedicated chaperone, NAC could sense and bind to the regulation-conferring segment, an event that presumably fortifies stalling.
claims.source: Conversely, if these are not swiftly enough captured by their dedicated chaperone, NAC could sense and bind to the regulation-conferring segment, an event that presumably fortifies stalling and, thereby, further decreases the speed of translation.
claims.evidence: This is a speculation about the consequence of delayed chaperone binding.

claims.claim: The findings are reminiscent of the observation that mammalian mRNAs encoding proteins whose signal sequence is inefficiently recognized by the signal recognition particle (SRP) are selectively degraded.
claims.source: Moreover, our findings are reminiscent of the previous observation that mammalian mRNAs encoding proteins whose signal sequence is inefficiently recognized by the signal recognition particle (SRP) are, albeit by a yet to be determined mechanism, selectively degraded (Karamyshev et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This draws a parallel to a similar mechanism in mammalian cells, citing Karamyshev et al., 2014.

claims.claim: The study highlights the r-proteins Rpl3 and Rpl4 as potential drivers of cellular protein aggregation.
claims.source: Notably, our study highlights the r-proteins Rpl3 and Rpl4 as potential drivers of cellular protein aggregation.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion from the aggregation experiments.

claims.claim: The aggregation of unassembled r-proteins represents a threat to the maintenance of cellular proteostasis.
claims.source: Our findings therefore further reinforce the notion that the aggregation of unassembled r-proteins represents a threat to the maintenance of cellular proteostasis, which, as shown by previous studies, yeast cells try first to avoid by clearing excess r-proteins via Tom1-mediated degradation (ERISQ pathway) and then to resolve by activating a stress response pathway, referred to as RASTR or RPAS, that increases the protein folding, disaggregation, and degradation capacity and decreases Ifh1-dependent transcription of RPGs (Sung et al., 2016a; Albert et al., 2019; Tye et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion reinforced by the study's findings, citing three references.

claims.claim: The reduced supply of single r-proteins, resulting in the accumulation of orphan r-proteins, causes proteotoxic stress and cell elimination in Drosophila.
claims.source: Importantly, the reduced supply of single r-proteins, resulting in the accumulation of orphan r-proteins, has also recently been shown to cause proteotoxic stress and cell elimination in Drosophila (Baumgartner et al., 2021; Recasens-Alvarez et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This cites recent findings in Drosophila, citing two references.

claims.claim: Mutations in around 20 different RPGs, mostly leading to haploinsufficiency of individual r-proteins, result in the development of Diamond-Blackfan anemia (DBA).
claims.source: Moreover, it is well established that mutations in around 20 different RPGs, mostly leading to haploinsufficiency of individual r-proteins, result in the development of a ribosomopathy called Diamond-Blackfan anemia (DBA) (Narla and Ebert, 2010; Danilova and Gazda, 2015; Da Costa et al., 2018; Aspesi and Ellis, 2019), whose defining characteristics include reduced proliferation and increased apoptosis of erythroid progenitor cells, raising the possibility that proteotoxic stress could contribute to the manifestation of DBA (Recasens-Alvarez et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This describes the connection between RPG mutations and DBA, citing five references.

claims.claim: Proteotoxic stress could contribute to the manifestation of Diamond-Blackfan anemia.
claims.source: Moreover, it is well established that mutations in around 20 different RPGs, mostly leading to haploinsufficiency of individual r-proteins, result in the development of a ribosomopathy called Diamond-Blackfan anemia (DBA) (Narla and Ebert, 2010; Danilova and Gazda, 2015; Da Costa et al., 2018; Aspesi and Ellis, 2019), whose defining characteristics include reduced proliferation and increased apoptosis of erythroid progenitor cells, raising the possibility that proteotoxic stress could contribute to the manifestation of DBA (Recasens-Alvarez et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is a speculation about the role of proteotoxic stress in DBA, citing Recasens-Alvarez et al., 2021.

claims.claim: Several unassembled r-proteins interact with the E3 ubiquitin ligase MDM2 and thereby inhibit the ubiquitination and degradation of the apoptosis-promoting transcription factor p53.
claims.source: Further, several unassembled r-proteins, especially RPL5 and RPL11 in the context of the 5S RNP but also RPL4 and RPL26, whose yeast counterparts are established Tom1 targets (Sung et al., 2016a; Sung et al., 2016b), interact with the E3 ubiquitin ligase MDM2 and thereby inhibit the ubiquitination and degradation of the apoptosis-promoting transcription factor p53 (Bursac et al., 2014; Pelava et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This describes the interaction between r-proteins and MDM2/p53, citing four references.

claims.claim: Both overexpression and depletion of RPL4 lead to p53 stabilization.
claims.source: In the case of RPL4, both its overexpression and depletion, the latter in an RPL5- and RPL11-dependent manner, lead to p53 stabilization (He et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This describes the effect of RPL4 levels on p53, citing He et al., 2016.

claims.claim: A possible connection between RPL3 and RPL4 variants and DBA is suggested by the identification of missense mutations in RPL3 and RPL4 in DBA patients.
claims.source: Moreover, a possible connection between RPL3 and RPL4 variants and DBA is suggested by the identification of missense mutations both in RPL3 (one DBA patient; His11 to Arg substitution, unknown significance for disease manifestation) and RPL4 (one individual with DBA-like phenotypes; Val-Leu insertion between Ala58 and Gly59) (Gazda et al., 2012; Jongmans et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This describes mutations in RPL3 and RPL4 found in DBA patients, citing two references.

claims.claim: Increased p53 activity plays a pivotal role in eliciting tissue-specific defects in a variety of different developmental syndromes.
claims.source: Besides in DBA, increased p53 activity also plays a pivotal role in eliciting tissue-specific defects in a variety of different developmental syndromes (Bowen and Attardi, 2019).
claims.evidence: This describes the role of p53 in developmental syndromes, citing Bowen and Attardi, 2019.

claims.source: In this respect, it is worth mentioning that genetic changes in HUWE1, encoding the ortholog of Tom1, are associated with multiple neurodevelopmental disorders, prominently including X-linked intellectual disability (Giles and Grill, 2020), and that reduced HUWE1 levels, due to a disease-causing mutation, increase p53 signaling (Aprigliano et al., 2021).

claims.source: Moreover, individuals with mutations in CNOT1 exhibit a broad range of neurodevelopmental phenotypes, most consistently resulting in intellectual disability, development, speech, and motor delay, and hypotonia (Vissers et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This describes the phenotypes associated with CNOT1 mutations, citing Vissers et al., 2020.

claims.claim: Perturbed proteostasis, elicited by unassembled r-proteins such as RPL3 and RPL4, could contribute to the development of DBA and possibly influence the aging process and be of relevance to the etiology of diverse developmental disorders and neurodegenerative diseases.
claims.source: Taking into account the findings of our study and the above considerations, perturbed proteostasis, elicited by unassembled r-proteins such as RPL3 and RPL4, could not only contribute to the development of DBA but possibly also influence the aging process and be of relevance to the etiology of diverse developmental disorders and even neurodegenerative diseases of protein aggregation (Kaushik and Cuervo, 2015; Szybińska and Leśniak, 2017; Maor-Nof et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is a speculation about the broader implications of the study's findings, citing three references.

results.result: Deletion of Caf130, Cal4, or NAC components suppresses the Δacl4 growth defect and increases RPL4 mRNA levels approximately twofold. The Btt1-containing NAC heterodimer provides the main contribution to suppression, especially at elevated temperature, while Egd1-containing NAC operates in a partially redundant manner.
results.evaluation: Claims C44-C50 are well-supported by genetic suppression data (growth assays) and qRT-PCR measurements showing ~2-fold increases in RPL4 mRNA levels in specific deletion mutants. The differential contributions of NAC β-subunits are demonstrated through systematic genetic analysis at multiple temperatures.

results.result: RPL3 mRNA exhibits similar regulation as RPL4 mRNA in Δcaf130, Δegd2, and Δbtt1/Δegd1 cells, but Cal4 deletion does not affect RPL3 levels. Δacl4 cells show decreased RPL4 and RPL3 mRNA levels, suggesting co-translational chaperone binding stabilizes these mRNAs.
results.evaluation: Claims C51-C54 are supported by qRT-PCR data showing differential regulation patterns. The specificity of Cal4 for RPL4 regulation and the inverse effect in Δacl4 cells provide strong evidence for the proposed stabilization mechanism.

results.result: The regulation of RPL3 and RPL4 mRNA levels occurs through mRNA stability rather than transcriptional changes. RNA-seq analysis reveals RPL3, RPL4A, and RPL4B are among the most prominently upregulated transcripts in Δcaf130 cells, with no other RPG transcripts showing similar upregulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C55-C60 are well-supported by ChIP-qPCR data showing no changes in RNA Pol II occupancy (C55), rapamycin treatment experiments (C56), and comprehensive RNA-seq analysis (C57-C60) demonstrating the specificity of regulation to these three mRNAs.

results.result: Not1 is naturally synthesized as two distinct protein isoforms in S. cerevisiae due to leaky scanning, differing by the presence or absence of the N-terminal 162 amino acids. These N-terminal residues are required for growth at elevated temperature and for mediating RPL3 and RPL4 mRNA regulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C61-C62 are supported by Western blot analysis showing two Not1 bands, mutagenesis experiments demonstrating leaky scanning mechanism, and complementation assays showing functional requirements of the N-terminal domain.

results.result: Deletion of Ccr4-Not core components (Caf40, Not3, Caf1, Ccr4, Not4) does not suppress the Δacl4 growth defect but instead synergistically enhances it. Caf40 and Not3 are not required for negative regulation of RPL4 mRNA levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C63-C65 are supported by systematic genetic suppression analysis showing no suppression and synthetic enhancement of growth defects. The conclusion about Caf40 and Not3 (C65) is a reasonable inference from the genetic data.

results.result: The Not5-NTD-mediated mechanism and several mRNA decay factors (Dhh1, Pat1, Xrn1, Ski2) are not part of the regulatory network controlling RPL3 and RPL4 mRNA abundance, as their deletion does not suppress the Δacl4 growth defect or increase mRNA levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C66-C70 are supported by genetic suppression analysis and qRT-PCR measurements. The negative results provide important specificity information about which pathways are not involved in the regulation.

results.result: GFP-Trap co-immunoprecipitation experiments establish that full-length Not1 co-purifies with Caf130, Btt1, and Cal4, but not with Egd1 or Egd2. The Not1.154C variant lacking the N-terminal 153 amino acids no longer co-purifies Caf130 and Cal4 but retains association with core Ccr4-Not components.
results.evaluation: Claims C71-C75 are well-supported by systematic GFP-Trap co-immunoprecipitation experiments with appropriate controls. The data clearly demonstrate the requirement of the N-terminal domain for Caf130 and Cal4 binding.

results.result: Yeast two-hybrid analysis reveals that Caf130 interacts with Not1, Cal4, and Btt1, but no direct interactions occur between Cal4-Not1, Cal4-Btt1, or Btt1-Not1/Cal4. Caf130 functions as a hub protein connecting Cal4 and Btt1 to the Ccr4-Not complex. At 16°C, Caf130 can interact with both Egd1 and Egd2.
results.evaluation: Claims C76-C81 are supported by comprehensive Y2H analysis testing multiple protein combinations. The hub protein model (C79) is a well-supported inference from the interaction data. The temperature-dependent interaction with Egd1/Egd2 (C80-C81) provides mechanistic insight.

results.result: Y2H mapping defines minimal interaction surfaces: Caf130 binds Not1 via amino acids 40-655, Btt1 via 292-655, and Cal4 via 686-938. Not1's minimal Caf130-binding surface (CaInD) spans amino acids 21-153. Btt1's minimal Caf130-binding region comprises the NAC domain (38-103) with a C-terminal extension. Both Caf130 and Egd2 bind to Btt1's NAC domain, suggesting mutually exclusive binding.
results.evaluation: Claims C82-C89 are supported by systematic Y2H mapping experiments with deletion constructs. The minimal interaction surfaces are well-defined through progressive deletion analysis. The mutually exclusive binding model (C88) is a reasonable inference from the overlapping binding sites.

results.result: The rpl4a.W109C allele and BIV mutations (W106A/R107A/K108A/W109A) robustly suppress the Δacl4 growth defect at all tested temperatures. These mutations restore RPL4A-yEGFP fusion mRNA levels in wild-type cells to levels similar to Δcaf130 cells, establishing W109 as a critical determinant for negative regulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C93-C96 are well-supported by growth assays at multiple temperatures and qRT-PCR measurements of mRNA levels. The genetic and molecular data converge to establish W109's critical role in regulation.

results.result: Mapping experiments identify amino acids 78-139 of Rpl4a as sufficient for negative regulation, with W109 as a critical determinant. Mutations abolishing Acl4 interaction further reduce RPL4 mRNA levels, suggesting co-translational Acl4 binding stabilizes the mRNA. Cycloheximide treatment abrogates the regulatory difference, confirming translation dependence.
results.evaluation: Claims C97-C101 are supported by systematic deletion mapping, mutagenesis, qRT-PCR measurements, and cycloheximide experiments. The data provide strong evidence for the minimal regulatory region and the role of translation in the regulatory mechanism.

results.result: The regulation-conferring region on Rpl3 is contained within amino acids 8-52, with residues F16 and L17 serving as main determinants for efficient negative regulation. The F16A/L17A double substitution enables normal growth and does not affect Rrb1 interaction.
results.evaluation: Claims C102-C105 are supported by systematic deletion mapping, mutagenesis, qRT-PCR measurements, growth assays, and Y2H interaction studies. The data clearly define the regulatory region and key residues.

results.result: Similar regulatory principles apply to RPL3 and RPL4 mRNA regulation, with maximal regulation requiring ~30 additional amino acids after the critical residues (F16/L17 for Rpl3, W109 for Rpl4). The nascent proteins harbor the regulatory signal, and co-translational chaperone binding precludes recognition by the regulatory machinery.
results.evaluation: Claims C106-C109 are supported by comparative analysis of mapping data for both proteins. The parallel regulatory mechanisms and the overlap of chaperone-binding and regulatory sites provide strong evidence for the proposed model.

results.result: Overexpression of Rrb1 or Acl4 increases RPL3 or RPL4 mRNA levels by >2.5-fold, while depletion of these chaperones decreases the respective mRNA levels by >2-fold. The availability of the dedicated chaperone is a crucial parameter for determining mRNA stability.
results.evaluation: Claims C110-C113 are well-supported by qRT-PCR measurements from overexpression and depletion experiments. The bidirectional effects provide strong evidence for the chaperone's role in mRNA stabilization.

results.result: Overexpression of Rpl3 or Rpl4 variants with deregulated expression (W109C, BIV, F16A/L17A, R19A/K20A/R21A) severely compromises growth of Δtom1 cells and leads to increased protein aggregation. Tom1-mediated clearance is required to prevent aggregation, with detrimental effects occurring once an aggregation threshold is exceeded.
results.evaluation: Claims C114-C121 are supported by growth assays, protein aggregation assays (Western blots of insoluble fractions), and dose-dependent effects. The data demonstrate the physiological importance of the regulatory mechanism in preventing proteotoxic stress.

results.result: Fluorescence microscopy reveals that mutant Rpl3 and Rpl4a variants display strong fluorescence signals in the nucle(ol)ar compartment of Δtom1 cells, indicating that induced overexpression leads to aggregation within the nucle(ol)ar compartment in cells lacking Tom1.
results.evaluation: Claims C122-C123 are supported by fluorescence microscopy experiments showing distinct localization patterns. The data provide spatial information about where aggregation occurs.

results.result: Cells simultaneously lacking components of the regulatory machinery (Caf130, Not1's CaInD, NAC subunits, or Cal4) and Tom1 are inviable. Genetic suppression analysis demonstrates that moderate (~2-fold) surplus of either Rpl3 or Rpl4 is sufficient to perturb growth and proteostasis in Δtom1 cells, with both proteins contributing to the synthetic lethality.
results.evaluation: Claims C124-C131 are well-supported by systematic genetic analysis including tetrad dissection, suppression experiments, and complementation tests. The data establish the physiological importance of the regulatory mechanism.

results.result: Tom1 depletion in Δcaf130 or Δcal4 cells leads to massive aggregation of Rpl3 and/or Rpl4 (detectable after 8 hr, extensive by 24 hr) and extensive perturbation of cellular proteostasis, with many additional proteins appearing in the insoluble fraction. The deregulated expression promotes aggregation and loss of proteostasis, accounting for synthetic lethality.
results.evaluation: Claims C132-C137 are supported by time-course protein aggregation assays, Western blot analysis, and mass spectrometry identification of co-aggregating proteins. The data provide strong evidence for the proteostatic consequences of deregulated expression.

results.result: The dedicated chaperones Rrb1 and Acl4 cooperate with the regulatory machinery to provide optimal levels of assembly-competent Rpl3 and Rpl4. By balancing de novo synthesis, pre-60S assembly can be sustained at high rates without requiring Tom1-mediated degradation. The main physiologically relevant targets are the RPL3 and RPL4A/B mRNAs.
results.evaluation: Claims C138-C140 are well-supported conclusions integrating multiple lines of evidence from the study. The specificity of regulation (C140) is demonstrated by RNA-seq data, and the physiological model (C138-C139) is supported by genetic and biochemical data.

results.result: The proposed model suggests that under normal conditions, Rrb1 and Acl4 capture nascent Rpl3/Rpl4 and stabilize the mRNA. When chaperones are sequestered, NAC interaction with the regulatory segment persists, enabling recruitment of the regulatory machinery, which likely promotes mRNA degradation via the Caf1-Ccr4 deadenylase module.
results.evaluation: Claims C141-C144 represent a speculative model in the Discussion section. While the model is consistent with the data, key mechanistic details (NAC interaction persistence, transfer to regulatory machinery, role of Caf1-Ccr4) lack direct experimental evidence and are inferred from the genetic and biochemical data.

results.result: Overexpression of Rrb1 or Acl4 leads to further increases in RPL3 or RPL4 mRNA levels, suggesting the chaperones are present in limiting amounts and that there is constant competition between chaperones and the regulatory machinery for nascent protein binding. Dedicated chaperones serve as molecular rheostats sensing pre-60S assembly status.
results.evaluation: Claims C145-C146 are supported by overexpression data showing further mRNA increases. The molecular rheostat concept (C147) is a well-supported interpretation integrating the chaperone availability, mRNA regulation, and assembly status data.

results.result: The meticulous adjustment of unassembled Rpl3/Rpl4 abundance may be essential for maintaining cellular proteostasis depending on the cell's proteostatic state. The autoregulatory feedback loop and ERISQ pathway constitute a robust buffering system to prevent harmful effects of excess Rpl3/Rpl4.
results.evaluation: Claims C148-C149, C160 are supported by the synthetic lethality data, aggregation experiments, and proteostasis perturbation observations. The data demonstrate the physiological importance of the regulatory system.

results.result: RPL3 and RPL4A/B genes contain category III promoters and show the highest Sfp1 dependence among RPGs. The co-translational regulation represents an elegant mechanism to reduce Rpl3/Rpl4 synthesis when unassembled levels exceed chaperone buffering capacity. The mechanism operates continuously under normal growth conditions, consistent with RPL3 and RPL4A/B transcripts having markedly shorter half-lives than other RPG mRNAs.
results.evaluation: Claims C150-C154 integrate prior knowledge (C150-C151, C154 citing published data) with the current study's findings (C152-C153). The continuous operation under normal conditions (C153) is supported by the basal regulation observed in wild-type cells.

results.result: Rpl3 and Rpl4 are among the earliest assembling large subunit r-proteins and fulfill a central role in compaction/stabilization of early pre-60S particles. Temporary nuclear storage in complex with dedicated chaperones provides buffering capacity for rapid response to assembly demand and connects assembly status to de novo synthesis rate. The regulatory mechanism enables more rapid response compared to transcription-based adaptation.
results.evaluation: Claims C155-C156 cite established knowledge about Rpl3/Rpl4 assembly timing and function. Claims C157-C159 are well-supported interpretations of the regulatory mechanism's advantages, integrating the study's findings with the biological context.

results.result: An involvement of Ccr4-Not core components in mRNA degradation can be supposed, with the Caf1-Ccr4 deadenylase module highly likely promoting RPL3 and RPL4 mRNA degradation. The utilization of a nascent polypeptide segment constitutes an unprecedented mechanism of Ccr4-Not recruitment to substrate mRNA.
results.evaluation: Claims C161-C163 are speculative statements in the Discussion. While the Caf1-Ccr4 involvement is plausible given the complex's known role in mRNA decay, direct evidence for its role in RPL3/RPL4 degradation is lacking. The novelty claim (C163) is reasonable but the mechanism remains to be fully demonstrated.

results.result: Heterodimeric NAC is involved in substrate recognition based on the requirement of both subunits. The NAC-β subunits may establish initial contact with the N-terminal part of the regulatory segment. Residues following key residues (F16/L17, W109) may promote nascent chain stalling. Timely chaperone association may preclude NAC interaction, while delayed capture allows NAC binding and fortified stalling.
results.evaluation: Claim C164 is supported by genetic requirements, but C165-C168 are speculative mechanistic proposals based on structural data from C. elegans and general principles of exit tunnel length. These represent reasonable hypotheses but lack direct experimental validation in the yeast system.

results.result: The study highlights Rpl3 and Rpl4 as potential drivers of cellular protein aggregation. The aggregation of unassembled r-proteins represents a threat to cellular proteostasis, which cells address through Tom1-mediated degradation (ERISQ) and stress response pathways (RASTR/RPAS).
results.evaluation: Claims C170-C171 are supported by the aggregation data in Δtom1 cells and integrate well with prior knowledge about ERISQ and RASTR/RPAS pathways. The data provide new evidence for Rpl3 and Rpl4 as aggregation-prone proteins.

results.result: The Discussion connects the findings to human disease, noting that reduced r-protein supply causes proteotoxic stress in Drosophila, RPG mutations cause Diamond-Blackfan anemia (DBA), and unassembled r-proteins interact with MDM2/p53. Mutations in RPL3, RPL4, HUWE1 (Tom1 ortholog), and CNOT1 are associated with various developmental disorders. Perturbed proteostasis from unassembled RPL3/RPL4 could contribute to DBA, aging, and neurodegenerative diseases.
results.evaluation: Claims C172-C181 accurately cite published literature connecting r-protein biology to disease. However, C174 and C182 are speculative proposals about potential disease mechanisms. While the speculation is reasonable given the study's findings, these connections remain hypothetical and require future experimental validation.

results.result: The Introduction provides established background knowledge about ribosome biogenesis, including ribosome composition, assembly complexity, r-protein production rates, biogenesis factors, structural advances, rRNA transcription and processing, RPG regulation, r-protein properties, quality control mechanisms (ERISQ, RASTR/RPAS), chaperone systems, nuclear import, dedicated chaperones, and autoregulatory feedback loops.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C2, C9-C40 represent background knowledge from the Introduction, appropriately cited from the literature. These claims establish the context for the study and are well-supported by the cited references.

results.result: The study's main findings are that co-translational recognition of Rpl3 and Rpl4 by their dedicated chaperones (Rrb1 or Acl4) reduces degradation of RPL3 and RPL4 mRNAs. Negative regulation occurs when chaperone availability is limited and nascent proteins are accessible to a regulatory machinery consisting of NAC and the Caf130-associated Ccr4-Not complex. Deregulated expression leads to massive aggregation and proteostasis perturbation in Δtom1 cells. The mechanism adjusts de novo synthesis to consumption during ribosome assembly, protecting cells from detrimental effects of surplus production.
results.evaluation: Claims C3-C8 represent the core findings stated in the Abstract. These are well-supported by the comprehensive experimental data presented throughout the manuscript, including genetic, biochemical, and cell biological approaches.

results.result: A common regulatory machinery subjects RPL3 and RPL4 mRNAs to co-translational downregulation when dedicated chaperones are unavailable. Central to the mechanism is the Caf130-mediated connection between NAC and the Ccr4-Not complex via Not1's N-terminal domain.
results.evaluation: Claims C41-C43 summarize key findings from the study. These are well-supported by the genetic, biochemical, and molecular data demonstrating the components and connections of the regulatory machinery.

results.result: The W109 residue is located at the C-terminal end of Rpl4a's long internal loop (amino acids 44-113), which mediates Acl4 binding. The Rpl4a.W109C protein still interacts with Acl4, albeit to a lesser extent than wild-type, indicating the W109 side chain is not strictly required for interaction.
results.evaluation: Claims C90-C92 are supported by structural knowledge (C90, citing published structures) and Y2H interaction data (C91-C92). The data demonstrate that W109 contributes to but is not essential for Acl4 binding.
